sections.heading: Beyond LASIK — A Safe Option for High Myopia

items.v:
If you’ve been told you’re not a good candidate for LASIK due to thin corneas, high myopia, or dry eyes, you’re not out of options. At OPTIMAX Eye Specialist, we offer the Implantable Collamer Lens (ICL) — a safe and reversible solution for long-term vision correction.
Unlike laser surgery, ICL does not remove corneal tissue. Instead, a biocompatible lens is gently implanted behind your iris and in front of your natural lens to correct your vision from the inside.

v: Over 1,000,000+ vision correction procedures completed
Experienced ICL-trained refractive surgeons
ISO-certified surgical suites with advanced diagnostic tools

sections.heading: What Is an Implantable Collamer Lens (ICL)?

items.v:
ICL is a micro-thin, flexible lens made of collamer, a biocompatible material that works in harmony with your natural eye. Once implanted, the lens corrects short-sightedness (myopia) and astigmatism without altering the shape of the cornea.
The ICL is invisible, does not require maintenance, and can be removed or replaced if needed.

v: Ideal for patients with high myopia (-6.00D to -20.00D)
Suitable for thin or irregular corneas
Does not cause dry eyes
Porcine-free (Halal) ICL available
Permanent but reversible

items.v: *A full consultation will determine your eye health and suitability for ICL.
ICL may be ideal if you:

v: Have moderate to severe myopia
Are not eligible for LASIK or PRK
Have dry eyes or thin corneas
Want a reversible vision correction option
Are aged 21 to 45, with stable prescription for at least one year

items.v: Eligibility is confirmed through detailed diagnostics and eye mapping.

no.heading: Who Is Not Suitable for ICL?

items.v: ICL may not be recommended if you:

v: Have advanced cataracts or glaucoma
Are currently pregnant or breastfeeding
Have chronic eye inflammation or infections
Are under 21 or over 45 with presbyopia (may benefit from alternative options)

items.v: Alternative solutions such as PRESBYOND or FLACS may be more appropriate.

ICL Procedure Steps
intro: How ICL Works — Step by Step:

items.title: Pre-op Eye Mapping
items.text: Corneal scans, anterior chamber depth, and pupil size measurement

items.title: Lens Customization
items.text: ICL ordered to match your eye anatomy

items.title: Lens Implantation
items.text: A tiny incision allows placement of the foldable lens behind the iris

items.title: Quick Recovery
items.text: Most patients resume normal activity within 24–48 hours

note: The procedure typically takes 15–20 minutes per eye and is painless.

groups.label: Before Surgery:
items: Stop wearing contact lenses as instructed
Complete pre-operative eye measurements and medical screening

groups.label: After Surgery:
items: Use prescribed anti-inflammatory and antibiotic drops
Avoid swimming and strenuous activities for one week
Attend follow-ups to monitor intraocular pressure and lens position
